title: Quantics tensor trains for multiloop functional renormalization group in multiorbital impurity models
abstract: The full frequency dependence of electronic interactions is central to dynamical correlations, but its numerical cost restricts multiorbital calculations. We formulate the multiloop functional renormalization group directly in the quantics tensor train representation, retaining all three independent vertex frequencies over broad ranges without an explicit high-frequency parametrization. Analytical tensor operators perform frequency transformations and internal summations without dense vertex intermediates. Multiloop corrections improve agreement of vertices and responses with independent references and reproduce the low-energy numerical renormalization group self-energy. Lower-temperature calculations resolve a quadratic frequency contribution to the analytically continued scattering rate. A degenerate two-orbital impurity exhibits distinct spin, orbital, and charge responses at fixed Hund coupling. In a compensated altermagnetic environment, an orbital-level splitting induces a local spin response despite zero magnetization of the unperturbed impurity. Increasing Hund coupling suppresses the orbital response while increasing its spin polarization. Renormalized one-particle propagation alone does not reproduce this strong polarization dependence. These results extend compressed multiloop calculations to dynamical correlations in multiorbital environments.
summary: This paper introduces a novel computational technique using quantics tensor trains (QTT) to perform multiloop functional renormalization group (fRG) calculations for multiorbital impurity models. This method overcomes the severe memory limitations associated with calculating full frequency dependence. The results demonstrate how strong electronic correlations, particularly via Hund coupling, induce complex, distinct spin, orbital, and charge responses in these correlated electron systems.
main_problem: The primary challenge is calculating the full frequency dependence of electronic interactions in multiorbital systems, which is computationally prohibitive using standard methods.
main_result: The authors successfully apply the multiloop functional renormalization group (fRG) using the quantics tensor train (QTT) representation, revealing distinct spin, orbital, and charge responses in impurity models.
method: The study employs the functional renormalization group (fRG) framework, specifically multiloop corrections, implemented via the novel quantics tensor train (QTT) representation to handle frequency dependence efficiently.
model_or_system: The work focuses on multiorbital impurity models, often related to the Anderson impurity model, where electronic correlations are governed by interactions like the Hund coupling. The calculations involve flow equations for the self-energy and two-particle vertex functions.
key_observables: Self-energy ($\Sigma_\Lambda$), two-particle vertex ($\Gamma_\Lambda$), dynamical charge and magnetic susceptibilities ($\chi_d, \chi_m$), and spin/orbital responses.
important_parameters: Hund coupling ($J/U$), temperature ($T/U$), and the regulator cutoff ($\Lambda$).
main_assumptions: The QTT formulation is presented as a numerical approximation to the underlying multiloop fRG equations, and the method retains the full three-frequency dependence without explicit high-frequency parametrization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the QTT representation for frequency transformations and compare storage requirements against dense vertex amplitudes. Supporting figures show the evolution of susceptibilities and self-energy differences as a function of Hund coupling and loop order.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the computational bottleneck of multiloop fRG, introduces the QTT method for efficient frequency handling, applies this to multiorbital impurity models, and presents detailed results on how spin, orbital, and charge responses are modified by Hund coupling and loop order.
why_interesting: The development of the QTT method provides a powerful, memory-efficient tool for calculating frequency-dependent correlation functions in strongly correlated electron systems, which is highly relevant for understanding complex materials physics.

(c) Storage requirements for the two-loop QTT representation and for six dense vertex amplitudes on grids with 𝑁= 2𝑅points per frequency axis. Dense storage is an estimate, not peak memory or runtime.

FIG. 4. Two-orbital Hund impurity at 𝐽/𝑈= 0.125 and 𝑅= 8 (𝑁= 256). (a) Spin, orbital-quadrupole, and charge interaction components along the flow; 𝑢increases as the regulator decreases at fixed 𝑈. Line styles distinguish one, two, and three loops. The orbital interaction changes sign along the flow, while the responses retain the hierarchy spin, orbital quadrupole, and charge.
